subject.title: fix(transcripts): imported text can inject terminal escapes through transcripts show

question: Should transcript plaintext presentation permanently use terminal-safe derived values—including directory-backed selectors—while raw provider session IDs remain canonical only in metadata, raw capture, and JSON output?
rationale: The patch closes a demonstrated terminal-injection path, but it also intentionally changes the public plaintext selector for non-safe provider IDs; the permanent raw-versus-derived boundary needs feature-owner confirmation rather than automated code repair.

options.title: Approve derived plaintext selectors
options.body: Merge the current contract: raw IDs remain canonical in metadata and JSON, while persisted summaries and plaintext CLI output use terminal-safe derived values.

options.title: Use reversible escaped selectors
options.body: Replace `safeSegment` presentation with an explicitly reversible terminal-safe encoding, accepting additional encoding and resolver complexity to preserve more visible identity.

options.title: Split selector policy
options.body: Land summary and stdout hardening separately while deferring the plaintext selector contract for a narrower follow-up decision.

recommendation.title: Approve derived plaintext selectors
recommendation.body: Merge the current contract: raw IDs remain canonical in metadata and JSON, while persisted summaries and plaintext CLI output use terminal-safe derived values.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available feature-history signal connects steipete to moving the transcript CLI, summary, and storage implementation into core.
